article.title: Representation Is Not Liberation
article.author: Melina Abdullah
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. “You’re not supporting Karen for mayor?!?!? Wow. That’s crazy!” Before I could make it in the door to the voter education event, a longtime sister-friend greeted me with those words of hello. Not a hug or a “thanks for coming.” My response? “I think it’s crazy to give away a billion dollars in raises to police, to appoint Jim McDonnell as chief, and to call it not-a-genocide in Palestine.” Days before the election, it is not my intent to write another column critical of the current mayor. I have tried to lovingly call her in with previous pieces in hopes of her changing course. That did not happen and I will vote accordingly. But this piece is not about Karen Bass. It is about reminding ourselves why we vote. At a time when access, being at tables and in rooms, is peddled as a reason to vote for candidates, we must remember that we are voting for policymakers, not prom queens. Our votes are not about who we like best or even who looks like us, but who is most aligned with or can be pushed to enact policies that advance our collective agendas, values, and vision. In many ways, election season is a time for self-reflection. We must ask ourselves what we actually believe in. What are our moral minimums? Many have asked me to produce a voter guide. There are some strong guides already in circulation. (I especially appreciate those published by the Black Los Angeles Young Democrats and Black Women for Wellness.) Rather than writing my own, I posted my moral minimums. Here is what I came up with. Related: The Black Panthers at 60: Black Liberation Was Never Just About Voting Black Lives Matter: Prioritize the liberation of Black people. When Black people get free, everybody gets free. F the Pol(ICE): Police descend from slavecatching, prisons from plantations, and ICE is a part of the larger infrastructure. There is no redeeming any of them. Point blank period. We want a strong robust community-based public safety system. Candidates who take money and endorsements from police associations are pledging their allegiance to them, and turning their backs on the people. Reparations Now: Reparations is a basic human right and core international legal principle. Black reparations must be paid to Black people for chattel slavery, the de facto slavery and segregation that followed, and every tentacle of Black oppression and dehumanization that remains and has yet to be dismantled. Free Palestine: Palestinians have a right to life and self-determination. Those who take money from the Israeli lobby condone genocide. They have no place. Free Palestine. Free Congo. Free Sudan. People over profits: Life and well-being are sacred. There is no thing or luxury more important than life. We have the collective right to good lives and to ownership over our own selves and beings. Workers’ rights over corporate greed. Liberated Ethnic Studies: We want an educational system that teaches our children the truth and empowers them as critical thinkers and informed actors. This means well-funded ethnic studies curricula and intentional, directed, school programs that provide critical supports. Free the land: Protect the planet. Support land-back to restore Indigenous stewardship. Advance Black autonomy. Related: Remembering Curtis Renee: Seven Lessons in Love, Liberation, and Revolution Solidarity forever: Stand in solidarity with Black people, Indigenous communities, LGBTQIA+ folks, women, workers, people with disabilities, the poor, and all oppressed people at home and around the world. I spent a few weeks reflecting to develop these. After posting on social media, others also weighed in. “What about environmental justice? Bodily autonomy? Ending sexual violence? What about stopping surveillance and the rise of the ‘stalker state?’ What do we do about Donald Trump and his legion of demons?” To be clear, this is by no means a complete list. There are glaring omissions here. But it is a start. Establishing and affirming my own moral minimums helps me not be duped by the tall Black man in the suit with a compelling life story running for City Attorney, who promises to prosecute protestors “only if they break the law.” Instead, moral minimums bring me to research who’s paying for John McKinney’s campaign and uncover millions in independent expenditures by cops, corporations, and MAGA groups. With just days to go before the ballot deadline. May we all reflect on our own moral minimums and use them to guide our vote. And then, the day after election day, let’s use them to guide our organizing and the necessary action to hold electeds accountable and do the real work of building the world that we all want, need, and deserve. The Los Angeles Sentinel
